```{r setup, include=FALSE}
project_root <- if (file.exists("R/site_level_cwd.R")) "." else ".."
result_path <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data",
  "site_level",
  "fluxnet_cwd_cws_pcwd.rds"
)
has_results <- file.exists(result_path)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi = 110,
  eval = has_results,
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

if (has_results) {
  result <- readRDS(result_path)
  site_order <- sort(result$site_summary$sitename)
}

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
)
```

  cat(

}

<style>

This vignette presents all FLUXNET sites that pass the ecosystem and data-quality
filters used by the source workflow and have at least 10 consecutive complete
years within the joint GPP/LE record. The network-wide figures summarize the
calibrated PET scalars and the annual relationships. Each site tab contains
separate plot tabs for the ET--PET calibration, CWD-bin distributions, and the
full-record daily CWD, PCWD, and CWS series.

The uncorrected latent heat variable (`le`, FLUXNET `LE_F_MDS`) is converted to
observed ET in millimetres. At each site, valid observed ET and
Priestley--Taylor PET days are divided into equal-width CWD bins. The initial
scalar is defined by the lowest-CWD bin as

\[
  \alpha_{site} =
  \frac{\operatorname{median}(\mathrm{ET}_{obs})}
       {\operatorname{median}(\mathrm{PET}_{PT})},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{PET}_{site} = \alpha_{site}\,\mathrm{PET}_{PT}.
\]

Bins 2 through 5 are then inspected sequentially. Whenever median observed ET
is greater than median scaled PET in bin (i), the scalar is recalculated as

\[
  \alpha_i =
  \frac{\operatorname{median}(\mathrm{ET}_{obs}\mid b \le i)}
       {\operatorname{median}(\mathrm{PET}_{PT}\mid b \le i)}.
\]

The final scalar therefore median-matches all observations from bin 1 through
the last bin that triggered a refit. In the limiting case this includes all
bins. The default is five bins and can be changed with `MCT_CWD_BIN_COUNT`. The
bins have equal width over each site's observed CWD range. Calibration days have
`LE_QC >= 0.8`, positive PT-PET, and non-negative observed ET. The copied
first-year spin-up used for CWD, CWS, and PCWD has already been removed from all
returned daily series. CWD is not reset on a calendar date. PCWD is reset on the
first day of the climatologically wettest potential-water-balance month.

## Site overview

```{r site-summary, results='asis'}
site_summary <- result$site_summary |>
  select(
    sitename,
    koeppen_code,
    igbp_land_use,
    year_start,
    year_end,
    nyears_overlap,
    cwd_bins_actual,
    pet_calibration_max_cwd_bin,
    n_pet_scalar_refits,
    pet_scalar,
    pet_calibration_cwd_min_mm,
    pet_calibration_cwd_max_mm,
    n_pet_calibration
  ) |>
  arrange(sitename)

cat('<div class="site-table">\n')
cat(
  knitr::kable(
    site_summary,
    format = "html",
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Site", "Köppen", "IGBP", "Start", "End", "Years",
      "CWD bins", "Final calibration bin", "Sequential refits", "PET scalar",
      "Calibration CWD min (mm)",
      "Calibration CWD max (mm)", "Calibration n"
    )
  )
)
cat("\n</div>\n")
```

## Calibrated PET scalars across all sites

```{r pet-scalars, fig.width=9, fig.height=10}
scalar_overview <- result$site_summary |>
  arrange(pet_scalar) |>
  mutate(sitename = factor(sitename, levels = sitename))

ggplot(scalar_overview, aes(pet_scalar, sitename)) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = 0, xend = pet_scalar, yend = sitename),
    linewidth = 0.45,
    color = "#8AB6D6"
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.1, color = "#0072B2") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", pet_scalar)),
    hjust = -0.25,
    size = 2.5,
    color = "grey20"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(0, max(scalar_overview$pet_scalar, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.12)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Site-specific median-calibrated PET scalar",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## Per-site annual correlations

For every site, the blue coefficient is the Pearson correlation between annual
maximum CWD as the response and annual maximum PCWD as the predictor. The green
coefficient instead uses preceding CWS as the predictor. Preceding CWS is the
maximum of the latest CWS event whose maximum occurs on or before the date of
annual maximum CWD.

```{r annual-correlations, fig.width=9, fig.height=10}
correlation_sites <- result$site_correlations |>
  arrange(correlation_cwd_pcwd) |>
  mutate(sitename = factor(sitename, levels = sitename))

correlation_long <- correlation_sites |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(correlation_cwd_pcwd, correlation_cwd_preceding_cws),
    names_to = "relationship",
    values_to = "correlation"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    relationship = recode(
      relationship,
      correlation_cwd_pcwd = "Annual maximum CWD ~ annual maximum PCWD",
      correlation_cwd_preceding_cws = "Annual maximum CWD ~ preceding CWS"
    )
  )

ggplot(correlation_long, aes(correlation, sitename, color = relationship)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey45") +
  geom_segment(
    data = correlation_sites,
    aes(
      x = correlation_cwd_pcwd,
      xend = correlation_cwd_preceding_cws,
      y = sitename,
      yend = sitename
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.45,
    color = "grey75"
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.95) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Annual maximum CWD ~ annual maximum PCWD" = "#0072B2",
      "Annual maximum CWD ~ preceding CWS" = "#009E73"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1), breaks = seq(-1, 1, by = 0.25)) +
  labs(
    x = "Within-site Pearson correlation (r)",
    y = NULL,
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## Per-site diagnostics {.tabset .tabset-pills}

Choose a site and then a nested plot tab to inspect its CWD-binned ET--PET
calibration, the corresponding within-bin flux distributions, or the complete
daily time series. These nested R Markdown tabsets provide the same folded
per-site organization as Quarto panel tabsets while retaining an installable
R-package vignette. The three cumulative water variables are overlaid in one
horizontally extended panel so that their timing can be compared directly.

```{r site-tabs, results='asis', fig.width=10.5, fig.height=4.2}
for (site in site_order) {
  site_meta <- result$site_summary |>
    filter(sitename == site)
  site_daily <- result$daily |>
    filter(sitename == site)
  calibration_bias_display <- ifelse(
    abs(site_meta$pet_calibration_median_bias_mm) < sqrt(.Machine$double.eps),
    0,
    site_meta$pet_calibration_median_bias_mm
  )

  cat("\n### ", site, " {.tabset}\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("#### Observed ET versus Priestley--Taylor PET\n\n")

  et_pet <- site_daily |>
    filter(
      is.finite(pet_pt_mm),
      is.finite(et_obs_mm),
      pet_pt_mm > 0,
      et_obs_mm >= 0,
      le_qc >= 0.8
    )

  bin_summary <- result$cwd_bin_summaries |>
    filter(sitename == site) |>
    mutate(
      cwd_bin = factor(cwd_bin),
      calibration_bin = as.integer(as.character(cwd_bin)) <=
        site_meta$pet_calibration_max_cwd_bin
    )

  et_pet_plot <- ggplot(et_pet, aes(pet_pt_mm, et_obs_mm)) +
    geom_point(color = "grey65", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.24) +
    geom_point(
      data = bin_summary,
      aes(median_pet_pt_mm, median_et_obs_mm, color = cwd_bin),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 3
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = filter(bin_summary, calibration_bin),
      aes(median_pet_pt_mm, median_et_obs_mm),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      shape = 21,
      size = 5,
      stroke = 1,
      fill = NA,
      color = "black"
    ) +
    geom_abline(
      slope = 1,
      intercept = 0,
      linewidth = 0.75,
      linetype = "dotted",
      color = "grey35"
    ) +
    geom_abline(
      slope = site_meta$pet_scalar,
      intercept = 0,
      linewidth = 0.85,
      color = "black"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = site,
      subtitle = sprintf(
        paste0(
          "scalar = %.3f; pooled bins 1--%d; refits = %d; ",
          "pooled median bias = %.2g mm d-1; n = %d"
        ),
        site_meta$pet_scalar,
        site_meta$pet_calibration_max_cwd_bin,
        site_meta$n_pet_scalar_refits,
        calibration_bias_display,
        site_meta$n_pet_calibration
      ),
      x = expression("Priestley-Taylor PET"~("mm d"^{-1})),
      y = expression("Observed ET"~("mm d"^{-1})),
      color = "CWD bin",
      caption = paste(
        "Outlined medians: bins used for final calibration;",
        "dotted: 1:1; solid: final calibrated PET scalar"
      )
    ) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1)))
  print(et_pet_plot)

  cat("\n\n#### Flux distributions by CWD bin\n\n")

  flux_by_bin <- site_daily |>
    filter(
      !is.na(cwd_bin),
      is.finite(pet_pt_mm),
      is.finite(pet_site_mm),
      is.finite(et_obs_mm)
    ) |>
    transmute(
      cwd_bin = factor(cwd_bin),
      PET = pet_pt_mm,
      `x × PET` = pet_site_mm,
      `Observed ET` = et_obs_mm
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(
      c(PET, `x × PET`, `Observed ET`),
      names_to = "flux",
      values_to = "mm_day"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      flux = factor(flux, levels = c("PET", "x × PET", "Observed ET"))
    )

  flux_boxplot <- ggplot(
    flux_by_bin,
    aes(cwd_bin, mm_day, fill = flux)
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(
      position = position_dodge2(width = 0.8, preserve = "single"),
      width = 0.7,
      linewidth = 0.3,
      outlier.size = 0.35,
      outlier.alpha = 0.18
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        PET = "#56B4E9",
        `x × PET` = "#D55E00",
        `Observed ET` = "#009E73"
      )
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste(site, "flux distributions by CWD bin"),
      subtitle = sprintf(
        "Equal-width bins; final scalar calibrated through bin %d (%d sequential refits)",
        site_meta$pet_calibration_max_cwd_bin,
        site_meta$n_pet_scalar_refits
      ),
      x = "CWD bin (lowest to highest deficit)",
      y = expression("Daily water flux"~("mm d"^{-1})),
      fill = NULL
    ) +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 12, r = 5.5, b = 5.5, l = 5.5))
  print(flux_boxplot)

  cat("\n\n#### Daily CWD, PCWD, and CWS\n\n")

  daily_long <- site_daily |>
    select(date, cwd_mm, pcwd_mm, cws_mm) |>
    pivot_longer(
      c(cwd_mm, pcwd_mm, cws_mm),
      names_to = "quantity",
      values_to = "mm"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      quantity = recode(
        quantity,
        cwd_mm = "CWD",
        pcwd_mm = "PCWD",
        cws_mm = "CWS"
      ),
      quantity = factor(quantity, levels = c("CWS", "PCWD", "CWD"))
    )

  time_series_plot <- ggplot(daily_long, aes(date, mm, color = quantity)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.27, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(CWD = "#0072B2", PCWD = "#D55E00", CWS = "#009E73"),
      breaks = c("CWD", "PCWD", "CWS")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste(site, "daily water-balance diagnostics"),
      subtitle = sprintf(
        "%d--%d (%d complete years)",
        site_meta$year_start,
        site_meta$year_end,
        site_meta$nyears_overlap
      ),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Cumulative water amount (mm)",
      color = NULL
    )
  print(time_series_plot)

  cat("\n\n")
}
```
